title: Roll a filled 18.5 kg glazed planter across a patio on the edge of its foot, onto a taped spot
instruction: Move the planter onto the taped square on the patio.
context: Moving a filled patio planter is an everyday garden chore. A 14-inch glazed pot full of moist potting mix weighs about 18.5 kg, and paving guides say to lift planters rather than drag them across the slabs. Without a dolly, people tip the pot onto the edge of its foot and roll it. Both hands on the rim hold it against falling back upright (about 7.8 N m at 22 degrees) and turn it like a steering wheel, staying well short of its 37-degree tipping point.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a sturdy table, each gripper's finger pads covered with nitrile finger cots. Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm; heights are above the table. Patio: two grey porcelain pavers, 60 x 60 x 2 cm (about 16 kg each), laid side by side across the table with a 5 mm grouted joint along x at y 0, near edges at x 16, far edges at x 76, spanning y -60.75 to +60.75; they don't move. Planter: an At Home 'Rolled White Ceramic Outdoor Planter, Large', white-glazed ceramic, glazed rolled lip 35.6 cm across and 3.2 cm thick, 30.5 cm tall, body 32.9 cm across at its widest (21 cm up), opening 29.2 cm inside the lip, unglazed foot ring 20 cm across with a rounded heel; 10.1 kg empty, filled with moist potting mix to 5 cm below the rim (about 15 L, 8.4 kg), 18.5 kg in all, centre of mass 15 cm up its axis. The mix is sealed in a tied heavy-duty plastic liner bag inside the pot, so nothing moist reaches the rim. Heading stripe: 24 mm blue painter's tape, 3 cm long, laid radially across the top of the rim on its left side (+y) at the start. It stands upright on the left paver, foot centre at (48, 12). Spot: 24 mm blue painter's tape on the right paver, a 40 cm square (inner edges 20 cm from its centre) around a cross 8 cm across, cross centre at (48, -12), 24 cm to the planter's right. Distractors, loose, ignored by the scoring: sunglasses (14.5 x 17.4 x 5.7 cm, plastic, 30 g) lying on the far left of the left paver at (68, 48); a glazed ceramic mug (11.4 x 9.0 x 8.0 cm, 350 g) on the far right of the right paver at (68, -48); a plastic bottle of water (6.8 cm across, 24.5 cm tall, 550 g) on the table beyond the pavers at (83, -34).
scoring: Read every control step (20 Hz). 0 for the rest of the trial if the planter ever tilts more than 32 degrees from vertical, if the lowest point of its foot ever rises more than 1 cm above the pavers (lifted), or if it has skidded more than 6 cm in all (dragged). Skid is read only while it rests: axis within 2 degrees of vertical, foot centre within 3 mm of the paver tops, moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 3 degrees/s. At the first and last moment of each rest, note the rim's centre and the bearing of the blue tape stripe on the rim. Travel of the rim's centre during a rest is skid in full (an upright pot can't roll). For each move between rests, skid is the rim centre's travel less 11 cm times the stripe's turn in radians (the smaller way round), not below 0; the turn counts only if the planter tipped at least 10 degrees during the move. Otherwise the planter counts only while standing: resting, with every fingertip at least 5 cm from it. Standing, its foot centre within 3 cm of the tape cross for 1 s: 1.0. Standing, foot centre within 8 cm of the cross (also while that 1 s runs): 0.5. Standing, foot centre at least 10 cm closer to the cross than at the start (24 cm away): 0.25. Not standing, or none of these: 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Real trial: tilt from a phone inclinometer logging on the planter's inner wall; lift, rests, hands clear and stillness from overhead and side video; the rim's centre and the stripe's bearing read on the overhead frames at the start and end of each rest, against the 40 cm tape square and a protractor overlay; at the end, before anyone touches it, a steel rule laid flat from the foot to the square's inner tape edge on all four sides gives the foot centre's offset from the cross.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Roll the planter back onto its start circle (a 20 cm pencil circle at (48, 12)) and turn it so the rim stripe is on its left (+y). Before each trial, weigh it on a bathroom scale (18.5 +/- 0.3 kg; adjust the sealed bag of mix) and check the bag's top is 5 cm below the rim and still tied, and the nitrile finger cots are intact.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies at 240 Hz. The planter is one rigid body of convex hulls from a lathe profile estimated from the listing; the bagged mix is part of it (no shift). Real size and mass, 18.5 kg. Foot on pavers: friction 0.7/0.6. The pavers are one fixed slab; tape is visual only. Nothing breaks or scratches: tipping, lifting and skid are read from the pot's pose. Finger cots aren't modelled; the demo caps grip at 40 N a finger.
